summary: Lower Array.prototype.push when the receiver is proven to be a normal, non-overridden array representation.

target.notes: The helper must append the value and return the new array length. A bare List<T>.Add call is not behaviorally equivalent because Add returns void.

semantics.notes: Native List<T>.Add may be emitted only when the result is proven unused and all other array semantics are preserved by the selected representation.

caveats: JavaScript arrays may be sparse or heterogeneous.
Array.prototype.push or the receiver's push property may be overridden.
Very large lengths and generic use of Array.prototype.push require separate handling.

tests.name: appends and returns new length
tests.input: const a = [1, 2]; const n = a.push(3); console.log(n, a);
tests.expected_behavior: prints a length of 3 and an array containing 1,2,3

tests.name: result ignored optimization
tests.expected_behavior: a contains 1,2; compiler may lower to the representation's native append operation if semantic analysis proves the return value is unused
